about.title: Livermore Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product does not care where it ends up. In Livermore, that might be a lithium battery that ignites on a kitchen counter, a ladder bought along Isabel Avenue that buckles, or an airbag that never deploys during a rear-end collision on I-580 Eastbound. When something you used as intended breaks and injures you, California law offers a path many people have never heard of: strict liability. You generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect, whether in its design, in how that specific unit was built, or in the warnings that came with it, and that the defect caused your injury. Manufacturers, distributors, and the Alameda County retailer who sold it can all share responsibility. The most useful thing you can do right now is keep the product, its packaging, and any receipt. LawProactive is a free service that connects Livermore residents with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: In many California product cases you do not need to prove anyone was negligent, only that the product was defective and caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with know how to frame a claim around that standard.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Matters
items.desc: The manufacturer, the distributor, and the store that sold the item may each be liable under California law. An independent attorney can identify who belongs in the claim rather than stopping at the first name on the box.

items.title: Preserving the Product Comes First
items.desc: A product liability case often turns on the physical item itself. Getting connected early means someone can advise you on keeping the product, its parts, and its packaging intact before anything is lost.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on I-580 in Livermore. Is that a product liability claim?
items.answer: It may be. Livermore recorded 364 injury collisions in 2025, and I-580 in both directions accounts for a large share of them, but a crash claim and a product claim are separate questions. If a safety system failed to work as designed, the vehicle or component maker could be liable regardless of who caused the collision. Do not have the car repaired or salvaged until an attorney has weighed in.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was careless?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, which means you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the maker tried hard to be careful is typically beside the point.

items.question: I threw away the packaging. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, but keep whatever is left, including the product itself, receipts, photos, and any order confirmation emails. Missing packaging can make identifying the manufacturer or the warnings harder, though not always impossible. An attorney can help track down model numbers and purchase records through the retailer or your bank.
